citations.claim: total energy exceeds allowed bound at first violating step
body falling with no controller work yet energy grew above initial

counterfactual.change: Changed only dt from 1/30 to 1e-4 (same 212 steps, all else identical); fine substeps remove the spurious energy gain so energy_bound passes.

explanation: A single elastic ball bouncing on the floor with large dt=1/30 and high gravity steadily gains mechanical energy with zero controller work. Positional correction / impulse at contact adds energy each bounce faster than gravity integration removes it, so total energy creeps from 150 J past the 170 J bound by step 212. With tiny dt the drift vanishes (energy stays ~150 J), pointing to contact/integration numerical energy injection at coarse steps.
vision_note: A single blue ball drifts slightly near the center of an otherwise empty arena from steps 209 to 211, then appears slightly lower in step 212. No wall contact, penetration, escape, waypoints, or dramatic jump is visible; the motion looks uneventful.
